source.citation: Willoughby et al., ACS Electrochem. 2 (2026) 353, Supporting Information
source.figures: embedded rasters, ~200 dpi; S4 is JPEG

method: Independent re-extraction of the six embedded figure images with pymupdf; own tick detection and label reading; own linear calibrations; stored points mapped back through my calibration and overlaid on the native image (verify_overlay.png per dataset, viewed); per-column comparison against my own colour-mask stroke medians, plus >=10 feature spot checks per trace (baselines, peaks, plateaus, decays, steps). Deviation = |stored - mine| in px / panel height in px. Columns where the stroke is vertical (extent > 8 px) are reported separately because a column median is ill-defined there.

checks.name: ratio_claims
checks.detail: Recomputed plateau ratios: m30/m44 0.29-0.33, m16/m44 0.13-0.22, m14/m28 0.0101-0.0116; m/z 14 sits only 2.0-3.5 px above zero, so the m14/m28 ratio is uncertain by roughly +/-30 % or more.

issues: Observation (verifier interpretation, not established): the N2 (S6c) and O2 (S6d, not extracted) calibration traces have identical time profiles and step times, and m/z 32 / m/z 28 = 0.24 in all three exposures while both fall by ~42 %. That is close to the O2/N2 ratio of air, and N2 m/z 28 (3.8e-9 A) is ~270x the N2O m/z 44 signal (1.4e-11 A) at nominally equal 1000 ppm despite similar RSFs (1 vs 1.13) and higher N2O solubility. The absolute N2 (and O2) sensitivities from S6 may be contaminated by air or a shared exposure; the m/z 14/28 fragment ratio is an N2 ionisation property and is less affected, but it is resolution-limited (above).

assumptions: Plotted flux is mol s-1 cm-2 of geometric area (axis 'mol/s*cm2'); the same area normalises j, so FE = z F * integral(flux dt) / integral(|j| dt) and the 0.196 cm2 area cancels.

N2O: 2NO3- + 10H+ + 8e- -> N2O + 5H2O, z = 8 per N2O molecule (4 per N). The flux is per N2O molecule (quantified against 1000 ppm N2O calibration gas), so z = 8 applies; z = 4 per molecule would halve FE_N2O (6.6-8.0 %).
Charge per cycle = 0.1 mA cm-2 x plotted pulse length (4.98-4.99 min) = 0.0299 C cm-2 (integrating the stored j trace gives 0.0301-0.0307, +0.4-2.5 %, because of the step columns).

Window = pulse start to next pulse start (cycle 5 to end of record, 56.68 min); trapezoid over stored column medians, no baseline subtraction (authors already baseline-subtracted; off-period values are floored at 0).
fe_recomputation_S1c.result: Cycles 1-4: NO 32.1-41.1 %, N2O 13.2-15.9 %, H2 1.7-4.6 %, sum 52.6-56.8 %. Matches the README (32-41 / 13-16 / 2-5 / 53-57) and meta within 0.2 points; cycle 5 (window truncated) 18.3 / 16.0 / 7.6 / 41.9 %.
fe_recomputation_S1c.units_discrimination: Reading the axis as mol s-1 (not per cm2) would raise all FEs by 1/0.196 = 5.1x (NO ~210 %), which is impossible, so the per-area reading is the only consistent one.
caveats: H2 FE is dominated by flux that persists through zero-current off periods after cycle 1; subtracting the pre-pulse level gives 0.1-3.5 % (cycles 2-4).

A single pre-pulse baseline also moves FE_NO by up to -7 points (cycle 3) because the NO tail from the previous pulse has not decayed; the README numbers are for the unsubtracted integral, which is the right convention for the units check.

interpretive_claims.claim: m/z 30 in 15N runs is not explained by 15N2O fragmentation; candidates 15N2 or 14NO from unlabelled nitrate
interpretive_claims.detail: Ratios recomputed and correct. Candidates are labelled 'interpretation, not established'; the 14NO option is explicitly set against the caption's H15NO3. The 0.1 x m46 fragment estimate relies on NIST N2O m/z 28/44 and is flagged as not reported in the SI. No overreach.

Supported by the m/z 30 excess and the weak m/z 15 test. Missing counterpoint (not an error): the 14N run's m/z 28 (S1a) shows no pulse-shaped rise, but its lower axis segment carries only a '0' label, so it cannot bound a 14N2 signal of roughly 8 pA (0.33 x the ~25 pA NO m/z 30 signal, assuming the same N2:NO ratio and sensitivity as the 15N2 hypothesis implies). The weak-test argument also depends on the S6c m/z 14/28 = 0.010-0.012, which is resolution-limited (2-4 px) and may come from an air-contaminated exposure (see S6 issues); with a larger N+/N2+ fraction the m/z 15 test would argue against 15N2.

interpretive_claims.claim: 14N and 15N runs are not replicates of one electrode state
interpretive_claims.detail: Potentials recomputed: -0.1 mA/cm2: 14N median -0.77 V (10-90 pct -0.92 to -0.56) vs 15N flat -0.79 V; -0.2 mA/cm2: 14N -1.45 V vs 15N -0.41 V. The inference is reasonable; a differing reference/iR treatment between runs is an alternative cause of the potential offset that the README does not mention.

open_issues: S1c/S2c H2 FE is background-dominated after the first pulse; treat H2 FE as order-of-magnitude only.
S5a m/z 31 15N2O-fragment trace is resolved only to ~1 pA (+/-50 %); not flagged in meta.

S6 N2/O2 calibration signals look air-like (m/z 32/28 = 0.24 constant, identical time program, ~270x larger than N2O at nominally equal ppm); absolute N2 sensitivity from S6 should not be used without the main text or raw data.

README doubt 1 could note that S1a m/z 28 cannot bound a 14N2 signal (single-label lower axis segment) and that the weak-m/z-15 argument depends on a resolution-limited, possibly air-derived m/z 14/28 ratio.
The 14N/15N 'not replicates' inference could also reflect different reference/iR handling; worth one clause if the README is revised.

Main text remains unread (whether it has IC/GC concentration time courses is unverified; the abstract only says GC, IC and EC-MS were combined; 15N enrichment also unread); the other uploads in the folder are Gao 2022 (ES&T) and a CV raw-data zip unrelated to Willoughby.
